questions.prompt: Which U.S. land deal with Mexico was completed in 1853?
questions.fact: The U.S. paid $10 million for a strip of what is now southern Arizona and New Mexico, wanted mainly because it was flat enough for a southern transcontinental railroad.

questions.prompt: What do chemists call a pure substance made from two or more elements bonded together?
questions.fact: A compound is chemically bonded, which is why water behaves nothing like the hydrogen and oxygen inside it. A mixture keeps its ingredients' properties.

questions.prompt: Which Olympic sport uses a bow and arrows?
questions.fact: Archery appeared at the Olympics in 1900, then vanished for 52 years. It only returned for good in 1972.

questions.prompt: In The Lord of the Rings, what object is Frodo tasked with destroying?
questions.fact: The Ring can only be unmade where it was forged, which is why the story is a journey into Mordor rather than a hunt for a weapon to destroy it.

questions.prompt: Which desert spans parts of Mongolia and China?
questions.fact: The Gobi is a cold desert. It sits high enough on the Mongolian plateau that snow sometimes settles on its dunes.

questions.prompt: What is the nation called in 'The Hunger Games'?
questions.fact: Panem takes its name from panem et circenses — 'bread and circuses' — the Roman phrase for keeping a population docile with food and spectacle.

questions.prompt: Which protocol name is commonly used at the start of website addresses?
questions.fact: HTTP stands for HyperText Transfer Protocol. The S in HTTPS means the connection is encrypted, which is why browsers now warn you when it is missing.
